title: Role of Mach number — Speed of Sound Activity
learningObjectives: Explain that the Mach number is the ratio of flow speed to the speed of sound in the gas.
Describe how the speed of sound depends on specific heat ratio, gas constant and absolute temperature.
Distinguish low-speed, transonic and supersonic conditions by the relative size of density and velocity changes.

explanations.text: The Mach number compares gas or flight speed to the local speed of sound and shows when compressibility becomes significant.

evidence.quote: The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

explanations.text: The speed of sound is the propagation speed of small isentropic disturbances and scales as the square root of gamma times R times T.

evidence.quote: The speed of sound is equal to the speed of transmission of small, isentropic disturbances in the flow.

explanations.text: At low subsonic speeds density changes are negligible, while near and above the speed of sound density changes match or exceed velocity changes.

evidence.quote: For the low subsonic conditions, compressibility can be ignored.
Compressibility effects become more important with higher Mach numbers.

predictions.prompt: Predict the speed of sound for air-like properties at room temperature.
Predict the speed of sound for a lighter gas at a cool temperature.
